summary: John W. Pettit is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed undergraduate studies at Haverford College, conducted doctoral work under Robert A. F. Thurman, and studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Lal Mani Joshi, Gunapala Dharmasiri, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

John W. Schroeder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After degrees at Los Angeles Valley College and the University of Oregon, including a PhD under Don Levi, he taught at Oregon, the College of Wooster, and St. Mary's College of Maryland.
John W. Spellman (1934–2021) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Washington (circa 1964–1967) and the University of Windsor (circa 1967–1999).

John Wilson (1804–1875) worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies after studying at the University of Edinburgh. He founded the Oriental Christian Spectator and Wilson College, and served as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai.

John Zavos is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He has held positions at the University of Manchester, including Lecturer in South Asian Studies (attested 2010) and honorary research fellow (attested 2026).

Join Saeki (1867–1952) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Sennyu-ji and under Jōchō Chihaya. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Kangakuin, Horyu-ji (serving as head 1903–1950), and the Japan Academy.
Joji Fujii (born 1947) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1966 to 1974 and later served on its faculty from circa 1989 to 2012.

Jokai Hiraoka (1923–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and held professorial posts at Shuchiin University and Otemae University (attested 1972 and 1987).

Jon Kabat-Zinn (born 1944) studied at Haverford College and MIT (Ph.D.). Active in religious studies and medicine, he founded the Stress Reduction Clinic and the Center for Mindfulness, and held posts at the University of Massachusetts from circa 1979 to 2000.

Jonardon Ganeri is a philosopher and Indologist who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal. He has held positions at King's College London, Nottingham, Liverpool, Sussex, Monash, NYU, and the University of Toronto.

Jonathan A. Silk works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. After earning his MA and PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez, he held academic appointments at Western Michigan, Yale, UCLA, and Leiden University.

Jonathan C. Gold is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He has taught at the University of Vermont, Drew University (attested 2006), and Princeton University (attested 2015–2016).

Jonathan Christopher Cleary (1947–2023) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed his doctoral work at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi (attested 1986) and served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.

Jonathan Geen is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his doctorate at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff by 2001. He has taught at McMaster University, Butler University, and the University of Rochester.

Jonathan Glover (born 1941) is a philosopher educated at Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served as a fellow and tutor at New College, Oxford (circa 1967–1998) and held posts at King's College London (circa 1998–2013) and the Hastings Center.

Jonathan Lear (1948–2025) was a philosopher who studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Rockefeller University (Ph.D.). He taught at Cambridge, Clare College, and Yale, before serving as a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago from 2014 to 2022.

Jonathan Mark Kenoyer (born 1952) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the Woodstock School and the University of California, Berkeley, he became a professor of anthropology at the University of Wisconsin-Madison circa 1985.

Jonathan Z. Smith (1938–2017) was a religious studies scholar educated at Haverford and Yale. He held faculty posts at Dartmouth, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Chicago, where he served as Dean of the College (1977–1982).

Jong-Nam Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Shitennoji University and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg by 1998 under Lambert Schmithausen, also studying under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Jongcheol Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Seoul National University and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima. He held posts at the University of Mysore (1992) and the Academy of Korean Studies (attested 2001).
